Commentary.Commentary: Right then, India have taken an unassailable lead in the series. This extends their unbeaten run at home in the T20I format to 17 series in a row without a loss. The caravan now shifts to Mumbai for the fifth and final game of the series, which will take place at the iconic Wankhede Stadium on Sunday, 2nd February. The game will begin at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). As always, you can join us early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The captain of India, Suryakumar Yadav says that it was a top effort from everyone in the field. Acknowledges the crowd and says that they were right behind them from the start till the end. Says that the boys know what brand of cricket they want to play. Feels that losing three wickets in an over pushed them back, but the way Hardik and Shivam Dube showed their experience was great. Feels that they are moving in the right direction. Also says that he was confident that between the 7-10 overs, they could control the game and Harshit Rana came in for them as the concussion substitute and delivered. On being asked about what to expect from Mumbai, he smiles and concludes by saying, 'A lot of fireworks'.
Shivam Dube is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his swashbuckling half-century. He is not available for the chat due to the concussion protocols and Suryakumar Yadav receives the award on his behalf.

The captain of England, Jos Buttler says that they started brilliantly in the Powerplay and should have gone on to win the game. Mentions that they did some really good things in this clash and it is disappointing not to have emerged victorious. Shares that he is happy with the brand of cricket they have been playing in this series.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Harshit Rana is up for a quick chat. He says that it was a dream debut for him. About his preparations, he mentions that he has been working hard and was waiting in the wings for a long time to prove himself. Says he got an opportunity this time and also says that bowling in the Indian T20 League has helped him a lot to develop as a bowler to bowl in the depth.

Earlier in the game, Jos Buttler won his first toss of the series and chose to bowl first. A triple-wicket maiden from Saqib Mahmood left India reeling at 12/3. Abhishek Sharma and Rinku Singh continued to play their shots, though that same aggressive approach eventually led to their downfall. Shivam Dube and Hardik Pandya then forged a solid recovery, with Dube taking on the role of the aggressor early on. Pandya soon joined in, and thanks to their fifties, India reached 181.

Despite losing Livingstone, Brook carried on his merry way and led the chase for England. However, lightning struck twice for England as they lost wickets in clusters. Earlier, they had gone from 62/0 to 67/3, and then from a promising position of 129/4, they slipped to 146/8. Jamie Overton kept the flame of the chase alive, and it came down to needing 25 off 12 balls. However, his departure on the last ball of the penultimate over effectively sealed the game for the hosts.

From that point, it was a proper arm wrestle as whenever England seemed to be gaining momentum, India responded by pulling them back. Harry Brook and Liam Livingstone got together and found the right approach, staying busy against the spinners to keep the chase moving ahead. Then came the most major talking point of the game - Harshit Rana was approved as the like-for-like concussion substitute for Shivam Dube, and he struck with his second ball.

India seal the series with a hard-fought victory! Time and again, they were pushed into a corner, but they held their nerve and came out on top. As for England, they had their moments in the game, and there were multiple occasions where they had India by the throat but just couldn't capitalize on their chances. In their pursuit of 182 runs, England got off to a blazing start thanks to Phil Salt and Ben Duckett. Duckett fell on the last ball of the Powerplay, and India capitalized on the momentum, sneaking in a couple more wickets to pull things back.

The ball travels flat and straight down the throat of Axar Patel who runs forward a few yards in from the deep, and takes a comfortable catch. Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! This game continues to ebb and flow, following the pattern we've seen so far. England got off to a flying start, and it looked ominous for India, but since breaking the opening stand, they have managed to claw their way back into the contest. Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full, on the stumps, Harry Brook defends it out safely. A successful over for India and Axar.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Axar Patel to Harry Brook, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Harry Brook comes out to bat.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Axar strikes now and both the English openers are back in the dugout in a very quick succession! This one comes in with the arm, and it is fired in quicker and flatter by Axar. Full in length, and right in front of the stumps, kisses the deck and skids through quickly, hurrying the batter into the shot. Phil Salt backs away and creates room to access the off side but exposes the stumps and plays all over it. The ball passes under the bat and crashes into the wickets. Phil Salt departs for 23 (21).
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Axar Patel to Phil Salt, OUT! b Axar Patel.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted one, and full at the stumps. Phil Salt drives back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Axar Patel to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length, outside off, Salt backs away and cuts it but finds the fielder at cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Axar Patel to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full, drilled down to long off for a solo.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Axar Patel to Jos Buttler, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! An appeal for stumping but not given. That in-drifter sliding down the leg side, Jos Buttler is on the back foot and tries to push it across to the leg side, but the ball keeps sliding on and beats the bat. Sanju Samson collects it safely behind the wickets and flashes off the bails in a snap. The side-on replay shows that Buttler never lifted his back feet in the air. But a sharp glovework by Samson.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Axar Patel to Jos Buttler, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Fired in quick, full and on leg, swept away neatly to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Axar Patel to Phil Salt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The captain of England, Jos Buttler walks in at number 3. Shivam Dube took a blow to the helmet while batting and has not taken the field yet. Ramandeep Singh was his substitute at the start of the innings, but Harshit Rana has now replaced him.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! Finally, India get something to smile on the last ball of the Powerplay! Bishnoi dishes out a deceptive back-of-the-hand googly and lands it fuller around off, Ben Duckett clears his front leg and looks to access the leg side, trying to go aerial. He is a bit too early through the shot and doesn't read the wrong'un out of Ravi's hand. Hence, a leading edge is found and the ball swirls over cover. Suryakumar Yadav keeps his eyes on the ball and takes a fine catch to his right. Ben Duckett departs for a quickfire 39 (19) and England end their Powerplay at 62/1. They are way ahead of India who were 47/3 at the same stage.
Commentary.Howout: c Suryakumar Yadav b Ravi Bishnoi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Ravi Bishnoi to Ben Duckett, OUT! c Suryakumar Yadav b Ravi Bishnoi.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding across off on a length, Ben Duckett mistimes his pull shot over the inner ring. The fielder, Axar Patel from mid on chases the ball as it keeps dribbling to the fence. He cuts it off and two runs are taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Ravi Bishnoi to Ben Duckett, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and flat on off, Phil Salt hangs back and punches it to cover where Suryakumar Yadav makes a half stop and parries the ball to the backward point region. A quick single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Ravi Bishnoi to Phil Salt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done! Easy-peasy says Salt! Serves a genuine half-volley on off, Phil Salt reads the googly and smashes it straight down the ground for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Ravi Bishnoi to Phil Salt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Drag-down, on top of middle and leg, Phil Salt backs away and punches it hard but finds the fielder at cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Ravi Bishnoi to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ravi Bishnoi is into the attack now. He begins with a flatter one, on middle and on a length, Phil Salt flat-bats it straight down the ground and it is cut off by Tilak Varma from long on. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Ravi Bishnoi to Phil Salt, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and quicker, going across, Ben Duckett shapes up to scoop it over the keeper by staying leg side of the ball but misses. An expensive start by Axar - 16 runs off his first over. England are off to a real flier. At the end of 5 overs, they are 53/0, needing 129 runs in 90 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Axar Patel to Ben Duckett, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! All the way! Slower and shorter, on middle and leg, Ben Duckett employs the switch hit again but has to reach out in front this time. He still manages to get the elevation and clears the deep backward point fence for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Axar Patel to Ben Duckett, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it through! On a fullish length, on middle and leg, Ben Duckett switches his stance and takes it on the full. Hits it past backward point for the second boundary of the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Axar Patel to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Speared in, on off, on a nagging length, knocked down to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Axar Patel to Phil Salt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! On the pads, slower through the air and the length is pulled back a bit, Ben Duckett has a swing at it but fails to connect. A leg bye is taken as the ball rolls off the pads in front of short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Axar Patel to Ben Duckett, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Duckett takes Axar on straight away! Darted across from around the wicket, on a length, Ben Duckett gets down and swats it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Axar Patel to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Will Arshdeep get his third? Nope. Spin in tandem now as Axar Patel is brought into the attack.
Floated up, fuller and on off, Phil Salt makes room to go back over the bowler's head. Ends up dragging it along the ground and it goes straight to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Varun Chakravarthy to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through by Varun, on middle, Ben Duckett goes for the switch hit again but does not quite middle this one. Hits it along the ground to the right of point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Varun Chakravarthy to Ben Duckett, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Slightly slower, on a nagging length, around leg, Ben Duckett backs away and swings for the hills but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Varun Chakravarthy to Ben Duckett, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Innovative and mighty effective! Sliding on, on a nagging length, on middle and leg, Ben Duckett brings out the switch hit and gets under the ball to hit it over backward point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Varun Chakravarthy to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Sees the batter backing away does Varun and he fires it in, on a nagging length, Ben slaps it straight to cover.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from around the wicket, attacking the stumps, on a nagging length, Ben Duckett blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Varun Chakravarthy to Ben Duckett, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Early signs of spin. Varun Chakravarthy is introduced into the attack. He replaces Hardik Pandya.
Another off-pace delivery, on a back of a length, Phil Salt punches it straight to backward point. Best over of the innings so far. 13 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arshdeep Singh to Phil Salt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Takes pace off, full and straight, at the stumps, Ben Duckett shuffles across for the scoop but there is no pace on the ball and he is a bit early into the shot. Toe-ends it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Ben Duckett, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Halt! The on-field umpire, Nitin Menon and Indian skipper Suryakumar Yadav are having a detailed conversation. Not quite sure what that is about. By the looks of it, it was an animated chat between the two. But for now, SKY goes back to his fielding position and we are good to go...

FOUR! A hat-trick of boundaries for Ben Duckett! This is an excellent start for England. Banged in short by Singh but this is not high enough to trouble the batter, Ben Duckett takes the short ball on and pulls it to the right of deep fine leg for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! In complete control this time! Fuller in length, at the stumps, at 136 kph, Ben Duckett brings his wrists into play and whips it over mid-wicket for yet another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Uppish but in the gap! Slanting into the left-hander, on a nagging length, Ben Duckett gets on his toes with a hop and jabs it uppishly but to the right of square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Ben Duckett, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in on the off stump, on a good length, Ben Duckett defends it solidly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Ben Duckett, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good work in the deep! Banged in short, over off and middle, Phil Salt swivels and pulls it all along the ground to the left of deep square leg. The substitute fielder Ramandeep Singh sprints and dives to his left to make the stop. Relays it to the converging deep mid-wicket fielder. Two runs taken.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely hit! 3rd boundary in 7 balls for Salt. On a length, pace off, on off, Phil Salt lets his hands flow into the shot and lofts it to the left of mid off for a boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on the pads, Ben Duckett nudges it to deep backward square leg for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace in the form of Hardik Pandya to operate from the far end.
Beaten! This is pushed across the right-hander, on a good length, Phil Salt stays leg side of the ball and looks to cut this one late but misses.
